title: Requirement
description: A statement of need that a system, component, or solution must realize, phrased as a specific, verifiable behavior or property (typically a 'shall/must' statement with acceptance criteria) and traceable to the stakeholders, drivers, or goals that motivate it. Use Goal instead when the statement expresses a high-level desired direction or end state that cannot be directly verified against a specific system, rather than a concrete need the system must meet. Use Constraint instead when the statement limits the design or implementation options (e.g. a mandated technology, budget, deadline, or regulation) rather than stating something the system must do or exhibit. Use Principle instead when the statement is a general normative rule that applies to all systems in a context and guides decisions, rather than a need assigned to a particular system or solution. Use Outcome instead when the statement describes a measurable end result the organization intends or has achieved, rather than a property the system must have to contribute to it.

documentation.description: Free-text statement of the requirement, including its full wording, rationale, source, and acceptance or verification criteria; set it whenever the name alone does not make the need verifiable.

requirementType.description: Classification of what aspect of the system this requirement addresses

x-dr-evidence: A requirements document, PRD, or SRS entry with a stable identifier (e.g. REQ-042, FR-7, NFR-3) and 'shall'/'must' wording
A user story or issue tracker ticket labeled as a requirement, with acceptance criteria that tests or reviewers check against
Test annotations, docstrings, or traceability matrices that reference a requirement ID (e.g. @Requirement("REQ-042"), '# Verifies NFR-3') linking code or tests back to the stated need
